title: Lesson 12 Overview
subtitle: Listen to the lesson explained in English

transcript.en: Hey! 👋 Welcome to Lesson 12 — More Furniture, the għ Past Tense & Old Shops.
Three things: **bathroom and living-room furniture**, the **past tense with għ verbs**, and Malta's **old shops**. Let's go!
The past tense rule is the same as before — the mamma plus a suffix for each person. This time the verbs have **għ** in the root.
When għ is at the **start** of the root, it stays put. 'He made':
When għ is in the **middle** of the root, the verb shifts more. 'He played':
But 'I played' drops that first vowel:
Same with 'switch on'. He switched on:
The trick: spot where the għ sits in the root, and you'll know how the verb behaves.
Old Malta had a specialist for everything. The barber:
And the grocery shop — ħanut tal-merċa — for everyday food. Notice 'ħanut' means shop, and 'tal-' tells you what it sells.
Furniture, the għ past tense, old shops. That's Module 4 complete. **Prosit!** 🇲🇹
